whatis.intro: Accounts receivable turnover counts how many times a year your customers pay off what they owe you. You get it by dividing credit sales by the average amount owed. Turned into days, it shows how long an invoice really takes to become cash.

cards.title: How fast, not whether
cards.body: A book turning 9.4 times a year can still hold a debt that will never be paid. The ratio measures speed, not the risk in any one account.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for collection speed rather than credit risk

cards.title: Which accounts it hides
cards.body: The ratio blends every customer, so the 8.8 days past terms could sit with one account or with all of them. An aging report by account shows which.
cards.alt: Magnifying glass, for the accounts the average blends together

cards.title: You sit in the middle
cards.body: You collect from accounts in 38.8 days, and that clock only starts once a case sells. Every day between paying your supplier and getting paid is cash you fund yourself.
cards.alt: Warehouse, for a distributor caught between account terms and supplier terms

who.h2: Who uses an accounts receivable turnover calculator
who.intro: Food distributors that sell to accounts on credit use it to see how fast those accounts pay. Whoever sets terms, grants credit or answers to a lender about cash should know the number.

look.h2: Inputs that bend a receivables turnover ratio
look.intro: The result rests on a handful of inputs. These three can shift it without anyone noticing, so check them first.

steps.title: A terms figure that fits the book
steps.body: The calculator takes one set of terms. If accounts run on a mix, weight the terms by credit sales before you enter them, or the days past terms will be off.

steps.title: Debt that will never be paid
steps.body: Balances you no longer expect to collect still sit in average receivables and drag the ratio down. Written-off debt has left it, so compare years on the same basis.

steps.title: The rate you actually pay
steps.body: The 9% should be what your credit line charges, or what the cash would earn. A guess there moves the yearly cost, though never the days.

vos.h2: Where VOS sits before the invoice
vos.h3: The order comes before the invoice
vos.body: VOS does not invoice, collect or keep your books. Its part comes earlier: customers review each line before sending, and each VOS app order carries a number, date and timestamp. If an account questions an invoice, you have a record of what was ordered and when.
